section_A.title: YOUR RAW INSTRUCTION
section_A.instruction: Generate a Phase 1 Implementation Playbook for the Stairway Configurator 2.0 upgrade. This is a sequenced, task-by-task markdown document that tells a developer exactly what to do, in what order, file by file. Each task must be small enough to complete, test, and commit independently. The playbook covers Phase 1 only: computation/geometry separation, constants extraction, Blondel comfort gauge, violation presets, historical annotations layer, dimensional uniformity toggle, and the stair type abstraction scaffold. Do NOT write implementation code — write the precise task instructions, file paths, type definitions, acceptance criteria, and dependency chain. The playbook must be grounded in the ACTUAL codebase architecture — use real file paths, real type names, real store names, real component names. Read the existing stairway-configurator.ts module config, the 3D Lab feature specification, the template system types, the store architecture, and the existing component library before generating any task. Three reference documents are provided as the feature's research, technical plan, and UX plan — use them as the WHAT and WHY but derive the HOW from the codebase. The playbook output file is: .ai/docs/01-product/stairway-configurator-v2-phase1-playbook.md

fields.product: SlateCamp — Interactive Learning Experience Platform (ILXP) for Philippine Architecture Licensure Examination (ALE) prep. The 3D Lab is a config-driven, template-based interactive 3D learning tool with 209 modules across 7 templates.
fields.tech_stack: Next.js 16 App Router, React 19, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, Shadcn UI, Supabase (auth + DB + storage), Zustand 5, React Three Fiber 9.5, drei 10.7, Three.js 0.183, tunnel-rat (SceneTunnel portal system)
fields.target_user: Filipino architecture students and practicing architects preparing for the ALE board exam. Primary device: mid-range 6" Android phone on Philippine 4G (10-15 Mbps). Performance target: 30fps sustained on Realme C55 / Samsung Galaxy A14.

doc_tree.01-product: Feature specifications — one file per major feature
doc_tree.02-architecture: System architecture, portal breakdown, DB schema, API reference
doc_tree.03-design: Design system, UX patterns, component library docs

existing_documents: .ai/docs/01-product/008-3d-lab-feature-specification.md — The authoritative 3D Lab feature spec. MUST READ FIRST. Contains: all type definitions (ParametricSceneConfig, GeometryInstruction, ViolationRule, AnnotationDef, ParameterDef, Preset), the template system architecture, the store architecture (11 stores), the component inventory, the file tree, and the rendering pipeline.

.ai/docs/05-reference/stairway-configurator-innovation-research.md — Research document covering 10 planned innovations with international code data, Blondel formula research, and prioritization matrix. USE AS: the WHAT and WHY for new features.

.ai/docs/05-reference/stairway-configurator-technical-implementation-plan.md — Technical architecture plan covering computation engine design, geometry pipeline rules, violation system, annotation system, interaction system, performance contract, state management, file structure, and hard do's/don'ts. USE AS: the architectural CONSTRAINTS and PRINCIPLES the playbook must follow.

.ai/docs/05-reference/stairway-configurator-ux-implementation-plan.md — UX & UI plan covering the Viewport Sanctity Rule, three-panel layout, violation preset system, component library integration (existing Shadcn components + 11 new components), microinteractions, and mobile responsive strategy. USE AS: the UX REQUIREMENTS the playbook must satisfy.
critical_source_files: src/app/dashboard/3d-lab/_config/modules/08-vertical/stairway-configurator.ts — The existing stairway configurator module config. ~896 lines. Contains: parameter definitions, geometry builder function, 22 violation rules across 4 Philippine laws, 8 annotations, 4 presets, and the parallel rule-set compliance architecture. READ THIS FILE IN FULL before generating any task.

src/features/3d-lab/types/templates.ts — Core type definitions for all templates. Contains ParametricSceneConfig, GeometryInstruction, ViolationRule, AnnotationDef, ParameterDef, Preset, CameraConfig, and the ModuleConfig discriminated union.
src/features/3d-lab/templates/ParametricScene.tsx — The parametric template that renders ParametricSceneConfig modules. This is what consumes the stairway configurator config.
src/features/3d-lab/templates/ParametricSceneRenderer.tsx — The R3F renderer that interprets GeometryInstruction[] arrays into Three.js meshes.
src/features/3d-lab/stores/useLabStore.ts — The combined Zustand store facade used by 3D Lab modules.
src/features/3d-lab/stores/createModuleStore.ts — The factory that creates per-module Zustand stores.
src/features/3d-lab/components/templates/ComplianceReportPanel.tsx — The existing compliance report UI component.
src/features/3d-lab/components/templates/ControlPanel.tsx — The existing parametric control panel component.
src/features/3d-lab/config/constants/ — Directory containing existing code constant files: pd-1096.ts, bp-344.ts, ra-9514.ts, nscp.ts, index.ts.
src/features/3d-lab/config/modules/08-vertical/ — Directory containing the 4 vertical transportation module configs.
hard_constraints: DO NOT modify the ParametricSceneConfig interface in types/templates.ts during Phase 1. All Phase 1 work must be backward-compatible with the existing interface. New types are additive only — extend, never break.
DO NOT modify ParametricSceneRenderer.tsx during Phase 1 unless extending GeometryInstruction to support new types. The existing renderer must continue to work for all 209 modules.
DO NOT break the existing stairway-configurator.ts export. The module must remain functional throughout all Phase 1 tasks. Each task produces a working state.

DO NOT use drei <Html> components inside the 3D viewport for text larger than 60px wide. This is the Viewport Sanctity Rule from the UX plan. Violation messages, code citations, and long-form text go in the ComplianceReportPanel, not in floating viewport overlays.
DO NOT introduce new npm dependencies without explicit justification.
DO NOT use useState or setState inside useFrame hooks.
DO NOT allocate new THREE.Vector3() or any Three.js objects inside useFrame or geometry builder functions.
Every new constant must include a code citation comment (e.g., // PD 1096 IRR Rule VIII §804).
Every new file must follow the existing naming conventions in the 3D Lab feature directory.
The computation engine (stairway-computation.ts) must be pure functions only — no Three.js imports, no React imports, no store imports.
Performance budget: <200 GeometryInstructions for straight-run, <30K triangles, <50 draw calls, <2ms computation time.
All Phase 1 tasks must work with the existing parametric template — no new template type.
known_open_decisions: The angular plane θ coefficient for BHL/AMVB computation requires verification against the full IRR text by a licensed architect before production deployment — this applies to DevControlsModule, not the stairway configurator, but flag if any cross-module dependency arises.
CAGE integration for in-canvas quiz is undecided — the playbook should note where quiz integration points exist but NOT implement quiz features in Phase 1.

The Viewport Sanctity Rule enforcement component (<ViewportContent> wrapper with dev-mode warnings) is defined in the UX plan but the implementation approach (React component vs ESLint rule vs both) is an open decision — flag it, don't assume.

The exact Shadcn component variants for the 11 new components (PresetChip, ComplianceLawCard, ViolationRow, etc.) need design system review before implementation — the playbook should define the component API but mark visual design as pending.
International code constants (IBC, ADA, IRC) need SME verification before production — the playbook should include the constants extraction task but mark all international values as UNVERIFIED.

section_C.title: THE META-PROMPT
section_C.description: AI instructions to produce the Phase 1 Implementation Playbook.
section_C.role: Senior prompt engineer, technical architect, and 3D Lab systems expert.
section_C.objective: Generate the Phase 1 Implementation Playbook as a sequenced, task-by-task markdown document. Every task must reference real codebase file paths, real type names, and real component names. The playbook is the bridge between the three reference documents (research, technical plan, UX plan) and the actual codebase — it translates architectural intent into executable developer instructions.

PHASE_0_DISCOVER.label: DISCOVER
actions: Scan .ai/docs/01-product/ for 008-3d-lab-feature-specification.md — this is the authoritative spec.
Scan .ai/docs/05-reference/ for the three stairway configurator reference documents (research, technical plan, UX plan).
Scan src/features/3d-lab/types/templates.ts for current type definitions.
Scan src/app/dashboard/3d-lab/_config/modules/08-vertical/stairway-configurator.ts for the existing module config.
Scan src/features/3d-lab/config/constants/ for existing code constant files.
Scan src/features/3d-lab/stores/ for current store architecture.
Scan src/features/3d-lab/components/templates/ for existing template components.
Produce a <doc_discovery> block listing all found files.
PHASE_0_DISCOVER.output_format:
<doc_discovery>
  spec_file: .ai/docs/01-product/008-3d-lab-feature-specification.md
  reference_docs: [list of found reference docs]
  source_files_read: [list of source files read]
  type_definitions_found: [list]
  stores_found: [list]
  constants_found: [list]
</doc_discovery>

PHASE_1_READ_AND_BASELINE.label: READ & BASELINE
actions: Read the 3D Lab feature specification IN FULL — extract: ParametricSceneConfig interface, GeometryInstruction type, ViolationRule type, AnnotationDef type, ParameterDef type, Preset type, the template routing system, the store architecture, and the component inventory.

Read stairway-configurator.ts IN FULL — extract: all parameter definitions with their defaults/ranges, the complete geometry builder function signature and logic, all 22 violation rules with their check predicates, all 8 annotations, all 4 presets, and the helper functions (mm, num, str, bool, isBP220, isAccessible, isExit, isHighOcc, isResidential, riserViolColor, treadViolColor, widthViolColor, strictestMinWidth).

Read the three reference documents — extract: the Phase 1 feature list, the computation engine architecture (ComputedStairState), the file structure plan, the constants naming convention, the Blondel formula details (2R+T, 600-650mm range), the violation preset registry (11 presets from UX plan), the Viewport Sanctity Rule, and the new component list.
Read existing constants files (pd-1096.ts, bp-344.ts, ra-9514.ts) to understand the current constant organization pattern.
Produce <spec_baseline> summarizing the current state of the stairway configurator.

PHASE_2_EXECUTE.label: EXECUTE
rules: Generate the playbook as a single markdown file at .ai/docs/01-product/stairway-configurator-v2-phase1-playbook.md.

Organize into numbered tasks. Each task has: title, objective, input files (to read), output files (to create/modify), dependencies (which prior tasks must be complete), detailed instructions, TypeScript type definitions or interfaces where applicable, acceptance criteria, and estimated complexity.
Task ordering must respect dependencies — no task references a file that hasn't been created by a prior task.
Every file path in the playbook must be a real path in the SlateCamp codebase following the existing directory conventions discovered in PHASE_1.
Every type definition must be compatible with the existing types in templates.ts.
Every new constant must follow the naming pattern found in the existing constants files.
Include a task dependency graph (Mermaid) showing the critical path.
Include a risk registry for each task (what could go wrong, mitigation).
Mark all tasks that require SME verification with ⚠️ NEEDS VERIFICATION.

PHASE_3_POST_UPDATE.label: POST-UPDATE
actions: Update .ai/state/current-task.md with the Phase 1 task list.
Update .ai/state/memory.md with decisions made during playbook generation.

block_1_system_context.title: SYSTEM CONTEXT
directives: You are a Senior 3D Lab Systems Engineer at SlateCamp. You have full access to the codebase.
Product: SlateCamp ILXP — an ALE exam prep platform with a config-driven 3D Lab containing 209 modules.
Tech stack: Next.js 16, React 19, TypeScript, R3F 9.5, drei 10.7, Three.js 0.183, Zustand 5, Shadcn UI, Tailwind CSS.

The 3D Lab uses a template system where module configs (TypeScript objects) are consumed by template renderers. The stairway configurator is a ParametricSceneConfig consumed by ParametricScene.tsx → ParametricSceneRenderer.tsx.
The .ai/docs folder is the single source of truth. Every task reads from it and writes back to it.
No roleplay, conversational filler, or meta-commentary. Output the playbook document only.

block_3_objective.title: OBJECTIVE
block_3_objective.directive: CREATE a new document at .ai/docs/01-product/stairway-configurator-v2-phase1-playbook.md. This is a Phase 1 Implementation Playbook — a sequenced, task-by-task guide for upgrading the stairway configurator from its current single-file config to a multi-file architecture with computation/geometry separation, enhanced presets, Blondel comfort gauge, and the foundations for Phase 2+ features. Every task must be independently committable and must not break the existing module.

00_header.title: Header
00_header.content: Title, date, version, status, links to the three reference documents, link to the 3D Lab feature spec.

01_phase1_scope.title: ## Phase 1 Scope and Goals
01_phase1_scope.content: What Phase 1 delivers, what it explicitly does NOT deliver (Phase 2/3 features), and the success criteria for Phase 1 completion.

02_current_state_snapshot.title: ## Current State Snapshot
02_current_state_snapshot.content: A precise inventory of the existing stairway-configurator.ts: line count, parameter count, violation rule count, annotation count, preset count, helper function list, geometry instruction count at default params. Derived from reading the actual file.

03_target_file_structure.title: ## Target File Structure
03_target_file_structure.content: The exact directory tree that will exist after Phase 1 is complete. Every file listed with its purpose. Must follow the existing 3D Lab directory conventions.

04_type_definitions.title: ## New Type Definitions
04_type_definitions.content: Every new TypeScript interface and type needed for Phase 1. Includes: ComputedStairState, StairTypeConfig, ComfortZoneStatus, PitchStatus, ComplianceResult, PerLawEvaluation, InternationalComparisonDelta, ViolationPreset. Each type must be compatible with the existing ParametricSceneConfig interface — extending, not replacing.

05_task_dependency_graph.title: ## Task Dependency Graph
05_task_dependency_graph.content: A Mermaid diagram showing all Phase 1 tasks as nodes with dependency edges. The critical path is highlighted.

06_task_list.title: ## Task List
06_task_list.content: Numbered tasks (Task 1 through Task N). Each task follows the per-task template below.

06_per_task_template.title: ### Task N: [Title]
fields: **Dependencies:** List of prior tasks that must be complete.
**Input Files (Read):** List of files to read before starting. Real paths.
**Output Files (Create/Modify):** List of files this task creates or modifies. Real paths.

**Detailed Instructions:** Step-by-step instructions. Reference specific functions, types, constants, and patterns from the codebase. If extracting code from an existing file, specify which lines/functions to extract.
**Type Definitions:** Any new interfaces or types this task introduces. Written as TypeScript code blocks.
**Acceptance Criteria:** Checkboxes. Each criterion is testable. Includes: TypeScript compiles, existing module still works, specific values are correct, specific patterns are followed.
**Estimated Complexity:** Low / Medium / High with justification.
**Risks:** What could go wrong and how to mitigate.

07_phase1_tasks_required.title: Required Phase 1 Tasks (generate one ### Task section per item)
tasks: Task: Extract Philippine code constants from stairway-configurator.ts into a dedicated constants file following the existing pattern in src/features/3d-lab/config/constants/. Include PD 1096, BP 220, BP 344, and RA 9514 stairway-specific constants with code citation comments.
Task: Create international code constants file for IBC 2024, ADA/ANSI A117.1, and IRC stairway values. Mark all values as UNVERIFIED. Follow the same naming convention as the Philippine constants.

Task: Create the stairway computation engine as a pure-function module. Extract all compliance logic from the existing stairway-configurator.ts violation check predicates and helper functions (isBP220, isAccessible, isExit, isHighOcc, isResidential, riserViolColor, treadViolColor, widthViolColor, strictestMinWidth) into pure computation functions. Add Blondel comfort formula computation (2R+T), pitch angle computation, stringer length, total rise/run, comfort zone status, and pitch status. Define and export the ComputedStairState type.

Task: Introduce the StairTypeConfig abstraction (straight only for Phase 1) into the type system. This is a scaffold — only the 'straight' variant is implemented but the discriminated union is ready for L-shape and U-shape in Phase 3.

Task: Refactor the stairway-configurator.ts geometry builder to consume ComputedStairState instead of raw parameters. The geometry function's signature in ParametricSceneConfig takes raw params, so create an internal adapter: the geometry function receives raw params, runs the computation engine to produce ComputedStairState, then passes it to the geometry sub-builder. This preserves backward compatibility with the ParametricSceneConfig interface.

Task: Add 11 violation presets to the stairway configurator presets array. The violation presets are defined in the UX plan (Section 5.3). Each preset must trigger exactly one primary violation and use the same Preset type from the existing interface. Organize presets into two groups using a naming convention: scenario presets (prefix: none) and violation presets (prefix: '⚠ ' or similar visual indicator in the label).

Task: Add the Blondel comfort formula as an 'info' severity violation rule and annotation. The comfort gauge appears as a new annotation entry in the annotations array. The 2R+T computation is performed by the computation engine. The violation rule fires when 2R+T is outside 600-650mm range with severity 'info'. The annotation displays the current 2R+T value. Since the existing ViolationRule type already supports severity 'info', this requires no type changes.

Task: Add historical context annotations. Create new AnnotationDef entries for historical/research context (Blondel 1672, Templer 1976, Cocoanut Grove 1942). These annotations use the existing visibleWhen predicate to show only when a 'showHistory' toggle parameter is active. Add the toggle parameter to the parameters array.

Task: Add dimensional uniformity simulation. Add a 'toleranceMode' toggle parameter and a 'toleranceRange' slider parameter (0-20mm, default 5mm). When tolerance mode is active, the geometry builder generates per-step riser variations using a seeded random function. Risers that deviate beyond 9.5mm from the flight's min/max get individual violation colors. This requires modifying the geometry builder's tread/riser loop but does not change the GeometryInstruction type.

Task: Create new UI components for the violation preset chip strip. Define the component APIs (props interfaces) for: PresetChip, PresetChipStrip, ViolationRow, ComplianceLawCard, ComplianceSummaryBadge, DimensionSlider, FixButton, LawActivationDot. Create the component files with proper TypeScript interfaces and basic implementations using existing Shadcn primitives (Badge, Button, Card, Toggle, Slider, ScrollArea). Add Storybook stories for each component.

Task: Integrate the comfort gauge into the Parametric template's DOM overlay layer. The gauge is a small corner-anchored HTML element (NOT a drei Html in the viewport) that reads 2R+T, pitch angle, and comfort status from the computation engine via the module store. It renders in the LabOverlayLayer or DOMOverlayLayer component. Must follow Viewport Sanctity Rule — max 120x60px, semi-transparent background, monospace font.

08_integration_test_plan.title: ## Integration Test Plan
08_integration_test_plan.content: A checklist of integration tests to run after all Phase 1 tasks are complete. Includes: existing 4 presets still work, all 22 existing violations still fire correctly, the module still renders in the 3D Lab browser, the module still works on the module detail page, performance budget is met, no TypeScript errors, no console warnings.

09_phase2_readiness_checklist.title: ## Phase 2 Readiness Checklist
09_phase2_readiness_checklist.content: What must be true for Phase 2 to begin. Includes: ComputedStairState is stable, StairTypeConfig scaffold exists, constants are extracted, computation engine is tested.

10_risk_registry.title: ## Risk Registry
10_risk_registry.content: Per-task risks aggregated into a single table with: risk description, likelihood (L/M/H), impact (L/M/H), mitigation strategy.

stages.STAGE_0: DISCOVER: Scan .ai/docs/ and src/features/3d-lab/ for all relevant files. Output <doc_discovery>.
stages.STAGE_1: BASELINE: Read all source files listed in critical_source_files. Read all reference documents. Read the 3D Lab feature spec. Extract the current stairway configurator architecture. Output <spec_baseline>.
stages.STAGE_2: EXECUTE: Generate the playbook markdown document. Every task must reference real file paths and real types from the codebase. Every type definition must be written as a TypeScript code block. Every acceptance criterion must be testable.
stages.STAGE_4: VERIFY: Run the verification checklist. Output <verification_result>.
stages.STAGE_5: CLOSE: Git commit with message: docs(stairway-configurator): create phase 1 implementation playbook

block_6_verification_checklist.title: VERIFICATION CHECKLIST
items: Every section from block_4 exists in the output document.
Every file path in the playbook exists in the codebase OR follows the existing naming convention for new files.
Every type definition is valid TypeScript that extends (not replaces) existing types.
Every task has all required fields from the per-task template.
The task dependency graph is a valid Mermaid diagram.
No task references a file or type that hasn't been created by a prior task.
The existing stairway-configurator.ts module remains functional after every task (acceptance criteria include backward compatibility checks).
All 22 existing violation rules are preserved — none are deleted or modified in ways that change their behavior.
All 4 existing presets are preserved.
The Viewport Sanctity Rule is enforced — no task introduces floating text boxes larger than 60px in the viewport.
All international code constants are marked UNVERIFIED.
The computation engine has zero Three.js or React imports.
Performance budget is referenced in acceptance criteria for tasks that add geometry.
.ai/state/ files have been updated.
Changelog has an initial entry.

block_7_hard_constraints.title: HARD CONSTRAINTS
items: DO NOT begin STAGE_2 without completing STAGE_0 and STAGE_1 — read the codebase first.
DO NOT fabricate file paths, type names, store names, or component names. Every reference must come from the actual codebase.
DO NOT modify the ParametricSceneConfig interface. Phase 1 is backward-compatible.
DO NOT introduce tasks that break the existing 209 modules.
DO NOT skip reading stairway-configurator.ts in full — the playbook must account for every helper function, every constant, and every pattern in that file.
DO NOT generate tasks for Phase 2 or Phase 3 features (nosing detail view, L-shape stair geometry, evacuation simulation, material selector). Only scaffold the abstractions they need.
DO NOT output conversational filler or explanations outside the playbook document.
DO NOT close without producing <session_delta> and updating state files.

update_rules: Add all Phase 1 tasks to ## Backlog with references to the playbook.
Add 'Stairway Configurator v2 Phase 1' as a project in ## In Progress.
Append under ## Decisions: decisions made during playbook generation (e.g., computation adapter pattern, preset naming convention).
Append under ## Constraints: all hard constraints from the three reference documents.
Append under ## Architecture Notes: the computation/geometry separation pattern, the ComputedStairState data flow, the stair type abstraction scaffold.

quality_criteria: Codebase Fidelity: Every file path, type name, and component name in the playbook exists in the actual codebase or follows its conventions.
Task Independence: Each task can be completed, tested, and committed independently without breaking the module.
Backward Compatibility: The existing stairway configurator works identically after every task.
Type Safety: All new TypeScript types are written as code blocks and are compatible with existing types.
Dependency Correctness: No task references artifacts from a task that hasn't been completed yet.
Research Grounding: Features are traceable to the research document (Blondel, Productive Failure, international codes).
Architecture Compliance: All tasks follow the principles in the technical plan (computation/geometry separation, pure functions, named constants, Viewport Sanctity).
UX Compliance: All tasks follow the UX plan (violation presets, three-panel layout, no viewport text blocks, component library integration).
Performance Awareness: Tasks that add geometry include performance budget checks in acceptance criteria.
